title: Eternal Night
sub: Most of the living world has never seen the sun
blurb: The ocean is almost all of the habitable volume on this planet, and almost all of that is deep water in permanent darkness. The lit layer everything you have ever photographed lives in is under two per cent of the column.

title: Four Degrees, Everywhere
sub: Tropical or polar, it makes no difference
blurb: The warm water you swim in is a skin a few hundred metres thick. Below the thermocline the temperature falls away and then simply stops changing: around 90% of the ocean sits between 0 and 4 °C, from the equator to the poles.

title: The Lure in the Dark
sub: A light, in a place with no light
blurb: The anglerfish dangles a glowing lure in front of a mouth that can swallow prey larger than itself. The glow is not hers: it comes from bacteria she houses inside the lure, and she cannot make it without them.
stats: can take prey larger than itself

title: The Male That Fuses
sub: He finds her once, and never lets go
blurb: In many anglerfish the male is a fraction of the size of the female. He bites on, their skin grows together, their bloodstreams join, and he is absorbed until little is left of him but his gonads. A female can carry several at once.

title: A Whale Fall
blurb: A dead whale reaching the floor drops more food on one spot than that patch of seabed would normally get in two thousand years. Sharks come first, then worms, then bacteria living on the oil in the bones — and some species are found nowhere else.
stats: species found only on whale bones

title: The Deepest Octopus
sub: Flapping along at seven kilometres down
blurb: The dumbo octopus swims by flapping two ear-like fins rather than by jetting. One was filmed in the Java Trench at 6,957 metres in 2020, the deepest an octopus has ever been seen. It has no ink sac — down there, there is nothing to hide from in a cloud of black.
